## Experiment: the fix is PROVEN (8 live trials, $1.92)

Rig: the Oracle-2 rig from 99d3, unchanged — disposable fixture repo (`/tmp/rutile/fixture`) in
which **every one of the six criteria is genuinely TRUE**, real `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`,
unmodified `completion_verifier.md`, the REAL shipped `wrap_completion_evidence_policy` with **no
injection anywhere**, `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, temperature 0.0, max_tokens 4096.

The **only** variable between arms is which `src` tree is imported. Arm A imports
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src` (byte-identical to `origin/main` for this file — verified by
`diff` against `git show origin/main:…` before the run); Arm B imports the patched worktree. The
oracle aborts if `completion_tool_policy.__file__` is not under the arm's tree, and both logs
carry that provenance line. `git diff --stat` between the trees: one file, 24+/8-.

### Results (N=4 per arm)

| metric | A = origin/main | B = patched |
|---|---|---|
| trials banking a false `met=false` | **4 / 4** | **0 / 4** |
| suppressed governed calls | 4 (1 per trial) | **0** |
| governed calls (mean) | 10.50 | **8.00** |
| run steps (mean) | 9.50 | **7.00** |
| verdicts recorded | 7 per trial | 6 per trial (= the manifest) |
| `UsageLimitExceeded` / any error | 0 | **0** |
| tokens in / out (arm total) | 324,704 / 7,485 | **242,587 / 6,589** |
| arm cost | $1.09 | **$0.83** |

Arm A is deterministic at temperature 0: in every trial the model batched at run_step 1, the
`read_file` for `src/demo/agent_call.py` lost the batch and was answered with
`COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` without executing, and c1 was later banked

> `met=false` — "Bounded repository search reached three unique evidence responses without
> demonstrating that this criterion is met; recorded met=false at the finite-search boundary."

against a file that exists and satisfies the criterion. Arm B recorded no suppression at all and
banked all six criteria correctly.

### Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (repro on unmodified policy)** — met: 4/4 baseline trials.
- **AC2 (fixed, >=4/4)** — met: 0/4 false unmet, all six criteria `met=true` from real content.
- **AC3 (no cost/step regression)** — met, and strictly better: calls 10.50 -> 8.00 (-24%), steps
  9.50 -> 7.00 (-26%), input tokens -25%, cost -24%, zero budget exhaustions. This is the
  expected sign: today a lost batch is paid for with an *extra round trip* (full context
  re-sent) that the fix removes, so executing the batched read is cheaper than steering it.
  It is also the direct refutation of the retry-storm risk the 99d3 counter-evidence
  established — suppressed calls go 1 -> 0 per trial rather than 6 -> 12 -> 49, because nothing
  here depends on the model choosing to re-issue.
- **AC4 (deterministic unit contract)** — met: `tests/unit/test_completion_tool_policy.py`,
  14 passing, including `test_parallel_evidence_batch_executes_every_evidence_call` and
  `test_batched_evidence_consumes_exactly_one_evidence_response`; the mixed-batch parametrization
  still asserts both steering directions between evidence and record.
- **AC5 (no surface change)** — met: `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` and every other notice constant are
  byte-unchanged, no prompt/tool-schema/CLI/MCP/library edit.

### The change

`src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py` only. The per-response claim becomes a per-*kind*
claim: `acted_steps: set[int]` -> `step_kind: dict[int, str]`. A step is claimed as `evidence` or
`record`; a further **evidence** call in an evidence-claimed step executes normally, while a
record sharing a response with evidence — and evidence sharing a response with a record — is
still steered exactly as before. The COMMIT discipline the claim exists to protect (a verdict
must never share a response with evidence gathering, and one verdict per response) is fully
intact; two read-only file reads never needed protecting from each other. The finite boundary is
untouched because `current_evidence_steps` is a set of **steps**, so N evidence calls in one
response still consume exactly one of the three — asserted deterministically by AC4's second test
and visible in Arm B's step counts.

Raw logs and per-trial JSON: `/tmp/rutile/{armA.log,armB.log,results_A_baseline.json,results_B_patched.json}`,
oracle `/tmp/rutile/oracle5.py`.

comments.body:
## CV failure-history review — ranked architectural shortlist (recommendations only, NOT implemented)

Reviewed ~45 CV-related tickets and the current tree. Fourteen distinct failure classes. Two
findings dominate and should frame any decision:

**Finding 1 — evidence *acquisition*, not judgement, is the fault surface.** Classes 1-8
(`bf31`/`4c2b` lying read tools, `c827`/`70bc` runaway loops, `9a08`/`1e88` budget exhaustion,
`5796` truncated-search-as-absence, `ed6d`/`8eb3`/`215f`/`2948` recovery failures, `0707`/`dd41`
banking protocol, `df3a`/`6f0a` output extraction, `1f19`/`003d`/`dc05` wrong tree) are all about
getting correct bytes in front of the model. In no ticket did the model read correct, complete
evidence and reason wrongly about it. `99d3` is the clean demonstration: the suspected
*judgement* fault was disproved over 22 live runs and the real defect was evidence starvation.
**Implication: spend reliability budget on the evidence path, not on the prompt or the model.**

**Finding 2 — OUTAGE is the modal failure and it has only one exit: `--force-close`.** "A
resource exhaustion is not a judgment that the work is incomplete" recurs verbatim across `10ae`,
`218e`, `8eb3`, `c827`, `ed6d`. With no third verdict state, every infrastructure failure
collapses into the unattested close the project forbids — **146 tickets carry a `FORCE_CLOSE`
audit record** (`502b`), and `c827` measured 20 of 205 epics force-closed. Meanwhile only four
confirmed FALSE METs exist (`0059`, `4b54`, `1019`, and `4636`'s `--ref` escape). **The gate's
operational cost is availability, not integrity** — so reliability work here is nearly free of
quality risk, which is unusual and worth exploiting.

A third pattern is a warning about method: **fixes to one class create the next class.** `0707`'s
three-response boundary — the progress guarantee that cured a zero-bank outage — is the exact
precondition for this ticket's false unmet. `bf31`'s tool fix removed the loop's fuel and
immediately exposed breadth exhaustion. Every remedy so far converts an outage into a
lower-rate false unmet. That is a defensible trajectory, but each new bound should ship with a
**starvation oracle** (what does this bound do when it fires on healthy work?) — this ticket's
Arm A is the template, and it cost $1.09.

### Ranked shortlist

**1. An INDETERMINATE verdict channel — separate "judged incomplete" from "could not finish."**
*Mechanism:* a third terminal state for resource exhaustion, provider outage, and truncated
search, recorded and signed as a non-judgment; the ticket stays unclosed but the run is
resumable, and `--force-close` returns to meaning *operator override* rather than *infrastructure
recovery*. `2eca` already built the precedent (exit 11, `resolution_class`, never-sign guard) for
provider outages; this generalizes it. `02a3`'s proposed `certified_pending_operator_attestation`
tri-state is the same shape and should be folded in.
*Reliability gain:* highest available — it addresses the modal failure of every outage class
(2,3,5,7,12) at once and removes the pressure that produced 146 force-closes.
*Quality risk:* none if INDETERMINATE can never satisfy the gate. *Cost:* zero extra LLM spend;
state-machine, signing, and CLI work only.

**2. Deterministic evidence prefetch — hand the model an evidence packet instead of making it
fetch one.** *Mechanism:* precompute the candidate file set from the ticket's `file_impact` plus
criterion text and inline it, leaving the tools available only for gap-filling. The decisive
datum is already on the tracker: `9a08`'s gold-context, no-tools control finalized the same six
criteria in **507 tokens / 7 seconds**, against a live agentic run of ~30k tokens / 468 s
(`1e88`). *Reliability gain:* very high — it collapses the loop class, the breadth-exhaustion
class, and the truncated-search class, because the evidence no longer depends on a growing
tool-call history. *Quality risk:* real but bounded — prefetch selection could miss evidence and
produce a false unmet; mitigate by making prefetch strictly *additive* (never restrict the tool
surface) and by measuring on the same oracle. *Cost:* substantially **lower**, likely the single
biggest spend reduction available.

**3. Evidence-integrity invariants enforced in the harness, with telemetry.** *Mechanism:* every
governed tool result the model receives must be either real tool output or explicitly typed as a
non-evidence control message, and the harness must count what it substituted — `suppressed_calls`,
`empty_result_returns`, `truncated_reads` — into the run sidecar. *Reliability gain:* high and
cheap; this is the generalization of the present bug. `bf31` (48% of `search_files` calls
returned a false `(no matches)`), `0707`, and `dd41` were all silent for months and would each
have shown up as a nonzero counter on the first run. It also converts "prompt says don't do X"
into "the harness makes X impossible," which is the lesson of `0707`.
*Quality risk:* none. *Cost:* zero LLM.

**4. Close the `coverage` gap on `verify-completion` (open ticket `fba8`).** *Mechanism:* the
`llm_step_failures` counter shipped for plan-review never reached the close gate, so a degraded
run is byte-identical to a clean one. *Reliability gain:* moderate but it guards the rarest and
worst class — `1019` is a confirmed **FALSE MET** where an `except Exception` degraded every one
of 32 provider calls to verdict `C` and the gate returned PASS, exit 0. Pair it with a standing
ban on any `except Exception` that can yield a verdict.
*Quality risk:* none. *Cost:* zero LLM.

**5. Resumable runs off the criterion bank.** *Mechanism:* a run that dies mid-way resumes from
banked verdicts rather than restarting; `2948` established the value (a run that had verified 20
of 22 criteria discarded all of them) and partially fixed it, but exhaustion still generally
restarts. *Reliability gain:* moderate-high; turns exhaustion into partial progress and composes
directly with recommendation 1. *Quality risk:* needs a freshness rule so a stale bank cannot
certify against a moved base ref — reuse the existing `verified_at_sha` discipline.
*Cost:* strictly lower (no repeated work).

**6. Extend content-addressed input discipline from the tree to the ticket snapshot.**
*Mechanism:* `1f19` fixed wrong-tree reads with `ref` + `verified_at_sha` in the signed manifest,
but the gate's materialized *ticket* snapshot can still lag `origin/tickets` — `show_ticket`
returning "Ticket not found" for a ticket already pushed, noted during `99d3` and **never
separately ticketed**. Same fix shape, applied one seam over. *Reliability gain:* moderate;
removes a residual false-unmet source. *Quality risk:* none. *Cost:* zero LLM.

**7. Re-file the surviving concern from `12b7`.** It was closed WON'T FIX because the *sharding*
design it proposed duplicated the fan-out `2948` had just deleted — but its actual concern, that
the CV is one aggregate agentic call whose history grows monotonically and sits on the wall-clock
critical path, was never re-filed. Recommendations 2 and 5 attack it obliquely; whether the
monolithic call shape itself warrants an ADR is an operator call. *Cost/quality:* n/a, this is a
request for a decision, not a change.

### Not recommended

- **Prompt-level remedies for evidence problems.** Measured twice and regressed twice: the
  affirmative re-issue notice (`99d3`: suppressed calls 6 -> 12 -> 49, one `UsageLimitExceeded`
  with no verdict) and the strict one-criterion-at-a-time prompt (`2948`: already-closed ticket
  `003d` flipped PASS -> FAIL; reverted).
- **Raising the step budget again.** `aec1` records that it was raised five times and a hard cap
  proposed twice, **every one of those decisions made without spend data**. Recommendations 2-4
  produce that data; the budget question should wait for it.
- **Any new actuator wired to `max_consecutive_repeat`.** `70bc` found the metric *inverted* — it
  scored a real 4-cycle 1 and a healthy run 5, and `a89d` had already drawn a wrong conclusion
  from it. Any detector gating real work needs a published confusion matrix first.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

A completion criterion backed by a file that genuinely exists can be banked met=false because
the verifier never obtains that file.

`src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py` (origin/main) enforces **one governed action per
model response**: line 124 holds `acted_steps: set[int]`, and lines 152-156 claim the step
before dispatch — the first governed call in a response wins, and every other governed call in
the same response returns `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` (line 154) **without being executed**.
Nothing re-executes the loser and nothing carries its result forward.

The cost is not one round trip, it is the criterion's evidence: the finite boundary at lines
166-172 counts **responses** (`current_evidence_steps`, line 162), so a response whose only
useful call was suppressed still burns one of the three. Three such responses bank
`met=false` via `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE` against a file that is present and correct.

## Evidence this is real (99d3 disproof rig, artifacts on 99d3)

Oracle 2 ran the **unmodified shipped policy** — no injection — over a six-criterion manifest
against a disposable fixture in which every criterion is genuinely TRUE. In **4/4 trials** the
model batched at run_step 1, a `read_file` for the c1 target lost the batch, and c1 was banked
`met=false` carrying the bounded-fallback evidence string. Oracle 4 showed the benign contrast:
when alternative tools still work the model recovers unaided (3/3 met=true), which is why the
defect is intermittent in production rather than constant.

## Constraint on the fix (measured counter-evidence)

Rewording the notice to instruct a retry was tested and **regressed**: suppressed-call counts
rose 6 -> 12 -> 49 across matched trials and one trial died `UsageLimitExceeded` with no verdict
recorded at all. Any remedy that depends on the model *choosing* to re-issue inherits that
risk. The remedy must be mechanical.

## Approach

Make the mutual exclusion **per kind, not per response**. The invariant that actually protects
the design is that a verdict record must not share a response with evidence gathering (COMMIT
discipline) — not that two read-only file reads must not share one. Concretely, replace the
`acted_steps: set[int]` claim with a per-step *kind* claim:

- A response's first governed call claims the step as `evidence` or `record`.
- Further **evidence** calls in a step already claimed as `evidence` **execute normally** and
  return real repository content.
- A **record** in a step claimed by anything, and **evidence** in a step claimed by a
  `record`, keep returning `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` exactly as today.

This is the limiting case of "re-execute the suppressed call": the call is never suppressed, so
recovery costs **zero** extra round trips rather than one. The finite boundary is untouched —
`current_evidence_steps` is a set of steps, so N evidence calls in one response still consume
exactly one evidence response. No prompt text, tool schema, notice constant, workflow key, or
public surface changes; `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` keeps its current wording so the measured
retry-storm lever is not pulled.

## Experimental protocol (results recorded as a ticket comment before landing)

Two arms on the identical Oracle-2 rig (real policy, real `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`, real
`completion_verifier.md`, bedrock sonnet-4-6, temperature 0.0), differing only in which `src`
tree is imported:

- Arm A = origin/main policy (baseline). Arm B = patched policy.
- N=4 trials per arm. Per trial record: governed call count, suppressed count, run steps,
  verdicts, and any criterion banked `met=false`.
- The fix is proven only if Arm B eliminates the false `met=false` on c1 while its governed
  call count and step count do not exceed Arm A's, and no trial exhausts its budget.

If the experiment does not show that, the change is not landed and the outcome is recorded here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A held-out live oracle running the **unmodified** shipped policy reproduces a criterion
      banked `met=false` whose backing file exists and satisfies it, caused solely by a
      governed evidence call that lost its response batch (baseline arm, >=4/4 trials).
- [ ] With the change, the same oracle on the same fixture banks that criterion `met=true` in
      every trial (>=4/4), citing real file content.
- [ ] Arm B's mean governed-call count and mean run-step count are **not greater** than Arm A's,
      and no Arm B trial raises `UsageLimitExceeded`.
- [ ] A deterministic unit test (no LLM) asserts that two `read_file` calls in one `run_step`
      both return real content, that `record_criterion_verdict` sharing a step with evidence
      still receives `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, that evidence sharing a step with a record still
      receives it, and that N evidence calls in one step consume exactly one of the three
      evidence responses.
- [ ] `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE`,
      `ALL_CRITERIA_BANKED_NOTICE`, the tool schemas, the reviewer prompt, and the CLI/MCP/
      library surfaces are unchanged.
- [ ] Existing completion tests, lint, typecheck, and full CI pass.
compiled_state.title: Completion verifier false unmet: suppressed governed read is never recovered
